In this video, I am going to answer a question I get all the time –  The kinds of tasks that I give my VA vary but they all have one thing in common. They are algorithmic. They are repetitive. However, there is some kind of a formula. So let me give you a few examples of some of the tasks that I give my VA. 
First off, they have daily tasks. Some of these tasks involve responding to emails. I tell explain that if the email says this, respond this way. There are a few emails that I get on a regular basis and I do not want to have to respond in the same way over and over again. So, I tell my VAs, “Hey, if you can respond to the email, great. Here are a few templates to use. Respond to the email if you can. If you cannot, put it in this special folder. I will check that folder.” So, if they cannot respond to an email, that is fine. But 80% of the time emails I get are repetitive or very similar so that my VA can handle them. 
Other tasks that they do are things like seeing what items we have in stock versus what items we do not presently have. I ended up creating an automated computer program that is able to determine this but originally we had to do this manually. Originally, we had to go into an Excel spreadsheet and search for which items we had in stock and compare that with sales. 
Another task which I was also able to turn into an automated computer program is when we get an order, we would have to put the instructions on a big piece of paper so the people that cut the fabric to be sewn were able to read the instructions easier. There were some reasons behind that but originally we had employees doing this by hand. Then we had employees typing it on the computer. We then had our VA do it and then ultimately we ended up designing a computer program they could handle it. Okay. Great. 
So, what other types of tasks am I going to be giving my VA for the new business that I will be launching soon? By the time this video is out, the new business may already be launched. I am going to be interviewing top people in the fitness health space with the goal of creating some kind of a connection with them. Now, I need to figure which people I should interview so I gave my VA a list of different keywords to type into iTunes and then 50 different tags or keywords, for instance, Paleo diet. I said type “Paleo diet” into iTunes and then 50 different podcasts would show up. I told my VA that for each podcast I want them on a spreadsheet which I provided. I told my VA to enter the name of the host of the website that is associated with the podcast, how many reviews it has, their email address, and their twitter handle onto the spreadsheet.
